examples.name: Sample — MonthlyTreasuryStatement_202509_p8
paragraphs: Twin pies sharing one legend, amounts printed beside the slices. Every slice name appears in both pies with a different value, so each pie is its own table under its own printed title, and the title is what tells them apart. Rows follow each pie clockwise from the top. The amounts are copied as printed — $1,581B with its separator, and ($60B), whose parentheses mark the Other slice of September as negative. The footnote under the legend is cut off at the bottom of the page and is elided.

examples.name: Sample — upstream_financial_review_2024_p9
paragraphs: A daily price curve with no printed name or values, and a triangle-marker series whose legend entry reads first-day-of-month price, all twelve of its values printed at the markers. The named series is the table's one column: 12 printed values, copied with their $. The daily curve has no printed name that could head a column — Jan alone also locates the marker series — so it gets no column. The two bold average statements are printed text, not data points, and follow the table.
